reasoning_content:
All six volumes exist. Installation is complete and verified:

1. ✅ Repository already cloned (pre-existing at /workspace)
2. ✅ Secrets generated (openssl x4, age keypair)
3. ✅ .env configured (ENVIRONMENT=production, domains, SCHOOL_SLUG, TRUST_PROXY, SMTP, AGE_RECIPIENT, all secrets)
4. ⚠️ Reverse proxy: not set up as a separate Caddy — no public DNS name exists in this environment. Since the base stack exposes no host ports (by design per the guide), the service is reached via the compose network. This is a documented design characteristic, not a failure. I'll note it as a deviation in the summary.
5. ✅ Stack started with `docker compose up -d --build` (re-run once after the ml-service download exceeded the health check start period — expected behavior per the guide)
6. ✅ Functionality checks: all 7 services healthy, migrate exited 0, API health pass, dashboard 200, Swagger UI served
7. ✅ School and admin teacher created via super-admin API (HTTP 201), verified in DB
8. SSO: optional, requires an external IdP — not set up (needs an external identity provider, out of scope for a self-contained install; documented as an admin task in the dashboard)
9. Moodle: optional — skipped per the guide ("Optional")
10. ✅ Backup: service reports schedule (not exiting), one-off run completes with age-encrypted archive (magic bytes "age-encryption.org/v1")

Additional bonus: full email OTP login loop verified end-to-end using a local SMTP sink (init 201 → email with code delivered → complete 201 → session).

Deviations/additional actions:
- Since public DNS/TLS names don't exist, domains are set to http://localhost:4000 / http://localhost:3000
- Instead of a Caddy reverse proxy, services are reached via the compose network (docker exec / curl container on workspace_default); the guide's proxy step is for a real school server with public DNS
- SMTP relay: a local Python smtpd sink container (mailcatcher alias) since no real SMTP relay is available
- age installed via apt for key generation
- The guide's `curl` commands were run via a curlimages/curl container on the compose network (busybox wget in the backend container lacks header-file support)
- One re-run of `docker compose up -d` needed because ml-service's initial model download exceeded the 5-minute health check start period (the guide states the initial start is slow; the first `up` gave up on dependency waiting — this is a known Compose limitation with long start periods)

Known environment gaps (documented, not failures):
- No reverse proxy with TLS: public URL access per the guide (https://api.../https://daz...) is not achievable in this sandbox (no public DNS). All in-network functionality verified.
- No external OIDC IdP (step 8 is an admin-side task in the dashboard; the backend's OIDC endpoints exist)
- No Moodle (optional)

The guide says functional checks from outside use a public URL. Since the sandbox has no public DNS, equivalent checks were performed inside the compose network. All verifiable claims pass.

Conclusion: SUCCESS.

Verification evidence:
- docker compose ps: all healthy, migrate exited 0
- /api/v1/health → {"status":"pass"...}
- dashboard /eckener-schule/login → HTTP 200
- swagger → 200 (6 mentions of swagger-ui)
- Backup: crontab loaded; one-off run exit 0; archive encrypted with age (magic bytes)
- School/teacher creation: HTTP 201, rows in DB
- Full email OTP login: 201 → mail with code 816780 in SMTP sink → complete 201

I'm confident in success. Writing the final report.
